text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Retailers association (GRTU) warns it will issue industrial directives to retailers if no agreement is reached with the government on cash registers. It is insisting the government should pay for modifications in the software of the registers to handle a new system that will replace VAT. The government is saying costs are minimal and should be borne by the owners.

-Office of Fair Competition appointed by the government to guard against profiteering. The appointment was made amid concern that some businesses might try unjustified profiteering when Malta changes from VAT to a new system of excise duties on July 1. Under the new system tax on services will be reduced from 15 to five percent but there will be a new five percent tax on products. Import duties for EU products remain unchanged at 15 percent, but they will rise slightly for products from outside the EU.

- Malta Drydocks workers hold demonstration. They were supporting relatives of nine workers killed in an accidental explosion at the yard two years ago. They are insisting that any compensation by the yard should not be linked to a court award for damages.
- Cost of living slightly up in April.
